newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian call money ends easy, gilt yields drop.
newsitem.headline: Indian call money ends easy, gilt yields drop.

text.p: Indian call money ended Wednesday easier on improved liqudiity while gilt yields dropped slightly in moderate trade, dealers said.
Call money ended in the 2.50-3.50 percent range, down from the day's opening quotes of 3.50-5.00 percent, they said.
"The availability of funds has definitely improved over the last couple of days," a dealer at a foreign bank said. "There seems to be more lenders in the market."
Easy call money spurred some buying interest in government securities although most of the day's trade was in a single security, dealers said.
"Out of a volume of abount 2.70 billion rupees traded on the National Stock Exchange today, about 1.14 billion was in the 13.55 percent 2001 stock," a dealer said.
The 13.55 percent govenment of India stock, auctioned on Tuesday, was traded above par on Wednesday, he said.
Dealers said the 13.50 percent 1997 stock was traded on Wednesday at a yield of 10.85 percent against its last traded yield of 10.89 percent.

"There was some buying interest in longer-dated securities also today," said a dealer. "But by and large, banks are still waiting to see how long the current easy liquidity will last before really taking positions in securities."
Treasury bills maturing in February 1997 were traded on Wednesday around 8.50 percent while longer maturity bills maturing in July and August were traded at 10 percent, dealers said.
There were no trades in certificates of deposit or commercial paper, they said.
